The NIST defines a cloud platform as having five inherent characteristics: on-demand self-service (users request their own VMs, sites, databases, etc, and they're automatically created), broad network access (widely accessible, multiple points of presence), resource pooling (getting economies of scale out of building a hosting "fabric" that provided services can share and be migrated on), rapid elasticity or expansion (users can request more services and they are transparently provided, without the user having to wait for more hardware to be ordered and installed), and measured service (users are charged for what they use - time a VM is running, bandwidth transfer, storage consumed, etc). Just renting a few servers in a rack is not a cloud service. Proving a database that clients connect to and put data into is not a cloud service (though it may run on a cloud service).
